purpose: Structured regional reasoning support for Keneflex. This file is not a diagnosis engine. It ensures the system considers clinically meaningful competing patterns before mapping a consumer to self-care or products.
principles: Consumer language first; clinical structure stays backstage.
Multiple patterns can coexist and should not be forced into one explanation.
Ask only questions that can change safety, likely pattern, treatment role, product requirements, or escalation.
A product recommendation is not allowed while a materially different unresolved pattern could require a different product or level of care.
Provider-specific instructions override Keneflex product choices.
Safety and product-label constraints are eligibility rules, not after-the-fact disclaimers.
sources: AAOS 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline on Management of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
American Society for Surgery of the Hand (ASSH) HandCare and Handthology resources
ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Chronic Hand and Wrist Pain

solution_implications: do not assume thumb-spica treatment
if mild self-care remains appropriate, neutral-position wrist support/night use may be a different role than thumb support
activity/setup modification may be relevant
persistent/progressive sensory or motor loss changes escalation
hard_stops: inability to reliably hold ordinary objects

consider_when: symptoms with elbow flexion or pressure
solution_implications: do not map automatically to a median-nerve or thumb-support solution
consider proximal versus wrist-level source before product selection

consider_when: sensory change not fitting one distal nerve
solution_implications: a local wrist/thumb product may not address the driver
consider professional evaluation when neurologic findings are persistent/progressive

consider_when: repetitive thumb or radial-ulnar wrist use
solution_implications: support role may require thumb-spica style stabilization rather than wrist-only support
activity/load modification is part of the plan
avoid unnecessary restriction if pattern does not support it

consider_when: intermittent swelling or reduced pinch strength
solution_implications: thumb-base support should match the joint role while preserving useful motion
adaptive equipment/load reduction may be part of total solution
coexisting nerve/tendon patterns may require separate handling
ordinary wrist/thumb brace may not address the primary mechanism
persistent locking may warrant clinician/hand evaluation
activity modulation and appropriately targeted splinting may differ from thumb-joint or nerve plans
do not substitute a thumb-focused support
trauma/instability/persistent mechanical symptoms may change evaluation threshold
a generic brace is not automatically the primary answer
rapid change, neurologic effect, or atypical features warrant evaluation
do not reduce to an ordinary overuse product problem
acute hot/red/swollen or systemic illness can require prompt evaluation
red-flag or fracture/instability suspicion supersedes commerce
do not mask an unresolved traumatic structural problem with a retail support
total plan may combine targeted support, recovery, setup/activity changes, and comfortable movement
ergonomic aids are considered only when they solve the identified load/setup problem
failure of a reasonable first plan should reopen the differential rather than trigger automatic product escalation
professional evaluation may be more appropriate than cycling through retail supports

questions: Have all plausible pattern categories that could materially change the product role or level of care been considered?
Is there any unresolved nerve, trauma, inflammatory/infectious, or structural pattern that would make the current retail plan inappropriate?
If multiple symptom locations behave differently, are they being carried as separate patterns?
Does the selected support type match the role required by the surviving pattern(s)?
Would a reasonable clinician looking at this history ask a materially important question Keneflex has not yet asked?
pre_recommendation_gate.rule: If any answer is yes/uncertain in a way that could change the recommendation, continue the work-up before presenting a product plan.
